Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Old `embeddable_hosts` site-setting values are interpolated unescaped into a raw SQL INSERT string, a SQL-injection-shaped pattern executed against admin-controlled but untrusted-for-SQL data during migration

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration builds a raw SQL string with `execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from the prior `site_settings` value (`embeddable_hosts[0]['value']` split by newlines). This value is not quoted/escaped via `connection.quote`/bind params, so a host containing `'` (or other SQL metacharacters) can break the migration or lead to SQL-injection-shaped execution during migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:3 — has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` has no `include: true`, so the JSON only carries `embeddable_host_ids`; store.js.es6's `_lookupSubType` looks for a top-level `embeddable_hosts` side-load array that is never emitted, so hydration silently produces `undefined` entries

adjudication.rationale: In `app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb` the association is declared as `has_many :embeddable_hosts, ... embed: :ids` but no `include: true` (or `embed: :objects`) is set. On the client side, `store.js.es6` hydration for `*_ids` explicitly maps IDs via `_lookupSubType(subType, type, id, root)` which requires the sideloaded top-level array (here `root.embeddable_hosts`) to exist; otherwise it will hydrate to `undefined` entries. The diff does not show any alternative mechanism that would ensure `embeddable_hosts` are sideloaded when only IDs are embedded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192 — Generalizing the hydration regex from `_id$` to `_id(s?)$` is a change to a shared, generic REST-response hydration helper: any existing `*_ids` field on any other rest_serializer:1 response (not just embedding) will now be silently deleted and replaced with a hydrated array, which is `[undefined...]` if no matching side-load array is present in root

adjudication.rationale: The diff does generalize store hydration from matching only `*_id` to also matching `*_ids` (`const m = /(.+)\_id(s?)$/.exec(k);`). In the new plural branch it always does `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []; delete obj[k];`, where `hydrated` is the result of `obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))`. If the expected sideloaded collection for that subtype is missing in `root`, `_lookupSubType` can return `undefined`, producing `[undefined, ...]` and the original `*_ids` key is still deleted. That behavior change is real and generic, but the diff does not prove that any existing non-embedding REST responses include `*_ids` without a matching sideload, so it’s an edge-case/compatibility concern rather than a definitively verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:153 — resources :embeddable_hosts` declares index/show/new/edit routes, but Admin::EmbeddableHostsController only implements create/update/destroy, so GET /admin/embeddable_hosts(.json) or GET /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id will error instead of returning a resource, an incomplete REST contract

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `resources :embeddable_hosts` under the admin namespace in `config/routes.rb`, which creates RESTful GET routes (`index`, `show`, plus `new`/`edit`) by default. But `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (new file) only defines `create`, `update`, and `destroy`—no `index`/`show` actions—so requests like `GET /admin/embeddable_hosts` or `GET /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id` would route to missing actions and raise an `ActionNotFound` error. The routes should be constrained (e.g., `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]`) or the missing actions implemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/site_settings.yml:759 — Removing the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` site settings drops them from the admin Site Settings API surface, breaking any external script/integration that reads or writes those keys via GET/PUT /admin/site_settings

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` keys from `config/site_settings.yml` and deletes their rows in the migration (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). That means these settings will no longer exist in the SiteSetting-backed admin site settings surface, and scripts calling the admin site settings endpoints for those keys would no longer be able to read/write them. However, this appears to be an intentional migration to the new `EmbeddableHost` model + admin UI/endpoints (`resources :embeddable_hosts`, `/admin/customize/embedding`), so it’s more of a backward-compatibility/API-change concern than an accidental defect.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from `site_settings` (`val.split("\n")`), any host value containing a single quote (or other SQL-special chars) will break the SQL (or worse), raising an exception mid-loop. There is no per-row error handling, so the migration can terminate before inserting all rows and before `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings ..."` runs, leaving a partially migrated state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:27 — Raw SQL string-interpolates `h` (from a pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` site_settings value) into an INSERT, a SQL-injection-prone pattern exploitable if that setting value was ever attacker/admin-influenced.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, the migration loops over `records.each do |h|` derived from `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts` and executes an INSERT via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Because `h` is not quoted/escaped via bind parameters or connection quoting, a value containing `'` or SQL could break out of the string and alter the SQL executed at migration time. This is a verifiable SQL-injection-prone pattern in the diff (even if only admin-influenced).

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:1 — Only a trivial subclass assertion exists; create/update/destroy actions (success, validation failure, not-found) have zero test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds non-trivial CRUD logic in `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` (e.g., `create`, `update`, `destroy`, and `save_host` handling params, defaulting `category_id`, and error rendering). However, the new spec `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` only asserts the controller subclasses `Admin::AdminController` and does not exercise any of these actions (success paths, validation failures from `EmbeddableHost` model validations, or missing-record behavior in `update/destroy` where `where(...).first` may return nil). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a proven runtime bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:1 — Only a trivial subclass assertion exists; `show`/`update` and the `fetch_embedding` OpenStruct assembly (id, embeddable_hosts ordering) are untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds Admin::EmbeddingController with nontrivial behavior: `show`/`update` render an `EmbeddingSerializer`, and `fetch_embedding` builds an OpenStruct with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)` (ordering matters). However, the new spec `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only asserts it subclasses Admin::AdminController and does not exercise `show`, `update`, or verify the OpenStruct assembly/ordering.
